title: Add Task Lighting to a Kitchen: Recessed Downlights and Under-/Over-Cabinet Fluorescents

locations.name: Brooklyn, New York, USA
locations.basis: Explicit mention in transcript: "Anytime you're in Brooklyn..."

summary: This Old House guides a kitchen-lighting upgrade in a small, low-light kitchen by replacing two ceiling fluorescents with recessed downlights and by adding task lighting from under and over the upper cabinets. The video follows the planning, cutting of ceiling openings, and wiring to run two recessed lights on one switch, then routing and powering thin fluorescent fixtures above and below the cabinet faces to provide clearer task lighting at the countertop. The crew navigates a ceiling obstruction (a bar for a former junction box) and a sprinkler-pipe drop, uses a template to size openings, and hides cords by trimming the cabinet face with an oscillating saw. The result is improved lighting on the workspace and a more ambient glow on the ceiling, demonstrated toward the end as the cabinet lights are tested along with the recessed cans.
topics: Pressure clips to hold recessed cans
Wiring two fixtures on a single switch
Power routing from switch to top of cabinets
Cable routing around studs and crown molding
Safety: turning off power before work

sections.title: Identify lighting deficiencies in a small kitchen
concepts: two overhead fixtures with separate switches
sections.description: Host notes the kitchen is small with limited light; two overhead fixtures exist but lighting is not task-oriented.

sections.title: Plan: recessed downlighting and single-switch control
sections.description: Vinny outlines removing the ceiling fluorescents and replacing with recessed downlights to bring light down to the working area; two fixtures will be tied to a single switch.

sections.title: Prepare ceiling for new fixtures (obstacles and safety)
sections.description: First steps include turning off power, disconnecting fixtures, and clearing an obstruction bar that held up a junction box.

sections.title: Hole enlargement and template use for recesses
sections.description: The team enlarges holes for new recessed cans using a template and pencil to guide accurate cuts.

sections.title: Install recessed cans and interconnect wiring
sections.description: Remodel recessed housings are inserted; pressure clips secure the cans; wiring is run between fixtures and joined with Y-nuts so both lights can be controlled together from one switch.

sections.title: Rethinking cabinet lighting: switch routing and placement
concepts: cable path to top of cabinets
sections.description: The existing wall switch will then control cabinet lighting; a snake is used to probe for a path, revealing a metal stud that requires routing near crown molding.

sections.title: Cabinet-lighting routing plan (revised path)
concepts: front vs back cabinet lighting orientation
sections.description: Power is planned to run up the wall to a new top-cabinet box and down to a second box beneath the cabinets; orientation is chosen to minimize bulb visibility.

sections.title: Under- and over-cabinet fluorescent lighting installation
sections.description: Fluorescent fixtures are installed above and below cabinets; the team places the back of the fixtures to minimize visibility of bulbs and uses front-side clips to secure them; an interconnect cable ties fixtures together.

sections.title: Cord concealment and final assembly
sections.description: An oscillating saw is used to trim the cabinet front so cords are hidden and present a clean knee-step for the installation.

sections.title: Power test and final result
sections.description: After wiring, power is restored and both recessed and cabinet lights are tested; the cabinet lighting provides a dramatic improvement and the episode ends with a Brooklyn location cue.
